$$ \frac{|\Lambda_{ij}|}{\sqrt{\Lambda_{ii}\Lambda_{jj}}}\leq\frac{|\Lambda_{ij}-\Theta_{ij}|+\Theta_{ij}}{\sqrt{[\Theta_{ii}-|\Lambda_{ii}-\Theta_{ii}|][\Theta_{jj}-|\Lambda_{jj}-\Theta_{jj}|]}}\leq K $$

for some constant $K>0$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\left|\frac{\Lambda_{ij}}{\sqrt{\Lambda_{ii}\Lambda_{jj}}}-\frac{\Lambda_{ij}}{\sqrt{\Theta_{ii}\Theta_{jj}}}\right| \displaystyle=\frac{|\Lambda_{ij}|}{\sqrt{\Lambda_{ii}\Lambda_{jj}}}\left|\left({\frac{\Lambda_{ii}\Lambda_{jj}}{\Theta_{ii}\Theta_{jj}}}\right)^{1/2}-1\right|\leq K\left|\left({\frac{\Lambda_{ii}\Lambda_{jj}}{\Theta_{ii}\Theta_{jj}}}\right)^{1/2}-1\right| \displaystyle\leq K\left|\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log p}\Theta_{ii}}\right)^{1/2}\left(1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log p}\Theta_{jj}}\right)^{1/2}-1\right| \displaystyle\leq K\left|1+\frac{2C}{\sqrt{\log p}}+\frac{C^{2}}{\log p}-1\right|\leq\frac{K^{\prime}}{\sqrt{\log p}} $$

for some constant $K^{\prime}>0$ . In the last to second inequality above, we use an elementary inequality $\sqrt{1+x}\leq 1+x$ for $x>0$ .

For the second term, by Assumption 4.1 (2), we have

$$ \left|\frac{\Lambda_{ij}}{\sqrt{\Theta_{ii}\Theta_{jj}}}-\frac{\Theta_{ij}}{\sqrt{\Theta_{ii}\Theta_{jj}}}\right|\leq C{|\Lambda_{ij}-\Theta_{ij}|}\leq\frac{C}{\sqrt{\log p}}. $$

We note that both the upper bounds in Equation (143) and Equation (144) do not depend on the indexes $i,j$ . Therefore, we have shown that $\max_{i,j\in[p]}\left|\Lambda^{0}_{ij}-\Theta^{0}_{ij}\right|\leq(K^{\prime}+C)/\sqrt{\log p}$ . This implies the claim in Corollary A.3.

$$ \sup_{t\in\mathbbm{R},(i,j)\in\Gamma^{c}}\left|\mathbbm{P}(M_{i}>t,M_{j}>t)-H^{2}(t)\right|\rightarrow 0,\ \ \ \text{as}\ n,p\to\infty. $$

$$ \displaystyle E_{1} \displaystyle=\Big\{\min_{j\in[p]}\Lambda^{(1)}_{jj}\geq c\Big\}\cap\Big\{\min_{j\in[p]}\Lambda^{(2)}_{jj}\geq c\Big\}, \displaystyle E_{2} \displaystyle=\Big\{\max_{i,j\in[p]}|\Lambda_{ij}^{0,(1)}-\Theta^{0}_{ij}|\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log p}}\Big\}\cap\Big\{\max_{i,j\in[p]}|\Lambda_{ij}^{0,(2)}-\Theta^{0}_{ij}|\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log p}}\Big\}, \displaystyle E_{3} \displaystyle=\Big\{||\Delta^{(1)}||_{\infty}\leq\epsilon\sqrt{c}\Big\}\cap\Big\{||\Delta^{(2)}||_{\infty}\leq\epsilon\sqrt{c}\Big\}. $$

The superscripts $(1),(2)$ reflects the data splitting step, and the corresponding random variables are defined on each part of the data. $c>0$ is some suitable constant (see Lemma A.14 and Assumption 4.1 (2)), and $\epsilon=p_{1}\log p/\sqrt{n}\rightarrow 0$ by Assumption 4.1 (1).

We consider the same decomposition as in Equation (89), and proceed to upper bound $I_{1}$ . Let $\rho=1/\sqrt{\log p}$ . Notice that for $(i,j)\in\Gamma^{c}$ , $\Theta^{0}_{ij}=0$ , thus we have

$$ \max_{(i,j)\in\Gamma^{c}}\big|\Lambda^{0,(1)}_{i,j}\big|\leq\rho\ \ \ \text{and}\ \ \ \max_{(i,j)\in\Gamma^{c}}\big|\Lambda^{0,(2)}_{i,j}\big|\leq\rho $$

once we condition on the high probability event $E_{2}$ . Let $\widetilde{Z}^{(1)}$ and $\widetilde{Z}^{(2)}$ be the normalized version (e.g. variance 1) of $Z^{(1)}$ and $Z^{(2)}$ (see Equation (20)), respectively, thus $\Lambda^{0,(1)}$ and $\Lambda^{0,(2)}$ are essentially the corresponding covariance matrices. We have

$$ \displaystyle I_{1} \displaystyle\leq\mathbbm{P}\left(\widetilde{Z}_{i}^{(2)}>I_{t}\big(T_{i}^{(1)}\big)-\epsilon,\widetilde{Z}_{j}^{(2)}>I_{t}\big(T_{j}^{(1)}\big)-\epsilon,T_{i}^{(1)}>0,T_{j}^{(1)}>0\right) \displaystyle=\mathbbm{E}\left[\mathbbm{P}\big(\widetilde{Z}_{i}^{(2)}>I_{t}(x)-\epsilon,\widetilde{Z}_{j}^{(2)}>I_{t}(y)-\epsilon\big)\mid T_{i}^{(1)}=x>0,\ T_{j}^{(1)}=y>0\right] \displaystyle\leq c_{1}\rho+\mathbbm{E}\left[Q\big(I_{t}(x)-\epsilon\big)Q\big(I_{t}(y)-\epsilon\big)\mid T_{i}^{(1)}=x>0,\ T_{j}^{(1)}=y>0\right] \displaystyle\leq c_{1}\rho+c_{2}\epsilon+\mathbbm{E}\left[Q\big(I_{t}(x)\big)Q\big(I_{t}(y)\big)\mid T_{i}^{(1)}=x>0,\ T_{j}^{(1)}=y>0\right] $$

for some constants $c_{1},c_{2}>0$ , in which the third line is based on the Mehler’s identity (see Equation (90)) and Lemma 1 in Azriel and Schwartzman, (2015), and the last line is based on the inequality in Equation (148). Similarly, we can upper bound $I_{2}$ , $I_{3}$ and $I_{4}$ . Combining the four upper bounds together, we obtain an upper bound on $\mathbbm{P}(M_{i}>t,M_{j}>t)$ specified as below,

$$ \mathbbm{P}\left(\text{sign}(W_{i}^{(2)}T_{i}^{(1)})f(W_{i}^{(2)},T_{i}^{(1)})>t,\text{sign}(W_{j}^{(2)}T_{j}^{(1)})f(W_{j}^{(2)},T_{j}^{(1)})>t\right)+4c_{1}\rho+4c_{2}\epsilon, $$

in which $W_{i}^{(2)}$ and $W_{j}^{(2)}$ are two independent random variables (also independent to everything else) following the standard normal distribution. We can further decompose the first term in Equation (156) into four terms as Equation (89) by conditioning on the signs of $W_{i}^{(2)}$ and $W_{j}^{(2)}$ , and repeat the upper bound in Equation (155). This leads to

$$ \mathbbm{P}(M_{i}>t,M_{j}>t)\leq H^{2}(t)+8c_{1}\rho+8c_{2}\epsilon. $$

Similarly, we can establish the corresponding lower bound. Thus we complete the proof of Lemma A.16.

#### A.7.1 Technical lemmas

#### Lemma A.18.

Under Assumption 4.2, for any $\epsilon>0$ , there exists a constant $C_{\epsilon}>0$ , such that $\mathbbm{P}(\cap_{i=1}^{4}E^{\epsilon}_{i})\geq 1-\epsilon$ , in which the events $E^{\epsilon}_{1},E^{\epsilon}_{2},E^{\epsilon}_{3},E^{\epsilon}_{4}$ are defined as below,

$$ \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{1}=\left\{\frac{1}{n}||X(\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star})||_{2}^{2}\leq C_{\epsilon}p_{1}\log p/n\right\}, \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{2}=\left\{||\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star}||_{1}\leq C_{\epsilon}p_{1}\sqrt{\log p/n}\right\}, \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{3}=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\gamma}_{j}-\gamma_{j}||_{1}\leq C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}\right\}, \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{4}=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\gamma}_{j}-\gamma_{j}||_{2}\leq C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}\right\}. $$

Proof of Lemma A.18. Lemma A.18 follows from standard arguments in Bickel et al., (2009), Raskutti et al., (2010), Bühlmann and Van de Geer, (2011), Van de Geer et al., (2014).

#### Lemma A.19.

Under Assumption 4.2, we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}\left|\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-\tau_{j}^{2}\right|=O_{p}\big(\sqrt{s\log p/n}\big), \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}\left|{1}/{\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}}-{1}/{\tau_{j}^{2}}\right|=O_{p}\big(\sqrt{s\log p/n}\big). $$

Proof of Lemma A.19. The proof follows similarly as the proof of Theorem 3.2 in Van de Geer et al., (2014), combined with some enriched arguments that we detail below. For any $\epsilon>0$ , we condition on the high probability event $\cap_{i=1}^{4}E^{\epsilon}_{i}$ . Since $X_{\widehat{\beta}}=W_{\widehat{\beta}}W_{\beta^{\star}}^{-1}X_{\beta^{\star}}$ , we have the following decomposition,

$$ \widehat{\tau}^{2}_{j}-\tau_{j}^{2}=\frac{1}{n}X_{\widehat{\beta},j}^{\top}\left(X_{\widehat{\beta},j}-X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right)-\tau_{j}^{2}:=I_{1}+I_{2}, $$

in which

$$ \displaystyle I_{1} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}X_{\beta^{\star},j}^{\top}\left(X_{\beta^{\star},j}-X_{\beta^{\star},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right)-\tau_{j}^{2}, \displaystyle I_{2} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}X_{\beta^{\star},j}^{\top}\left(W^{2}_{\widehat{\beta}}W_{\beta^{\star}}^{-2}-I\right)\left(X_{\beta^{\star},j}-X_{\beta^{\star},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right). $$

We proceed to upper bound $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ .

We further decompose $I_{1}$ into four terms, $I_{1}=I_{11}+I_{12}+I_{13}+I_{14}$ , in which

$$ \displaystyle I_{11} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\eta_{i}^{\top}\eta_{j}-\tau_{j}^{2}, \displaystyle I_{12} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\eta_{j}^{\top}X_{\beta^{\star},-j}(\gamma_{j}-\widehat{\gamma}_{j}), \displaystyle I_{13} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\gamma_{j}^{\top}X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}^{\top}\left(X_{\widehat{\beta},j}-X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right), \displaystyle I_{14} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\gamma_{j}^{\top}X_{\beta^{\star},-j}^{\top}\left(I-W^{2}_{\widehat{\beta}}W_{\beta^{\star}}^{-2}\right)\left(X_{\beta^{\star},j}-X_{\beta^{\star},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right). $$

For $I_{11}$ , by Assumption 4.2 (2), we have

$$ ||\eta_{j}||_{\infty}\leq||X_{\beta^{\star},j}||_{\infty}+||X_{\beta^{\star},-j}\gamma_{j}||_{\infty}\leq 2C_{1}. $$

Since $\mathbbm{E}[\eta_{j}^{\top}\eta_{j}/n]=\tau_{j}^{2}$ , we have

$$ \max_{j\in[p]}I_{11}=O_{p}(\sqrt{\log p/n}), $$

based on the union bound and the Hoeffding’s inequality.

For $I_{12}$ , since $\mathbbm{E}[\eta_{j}^{\top}X_{\beta^{\star},-j}]=0$ , we have

$$ \max_{j\in[p]}||\eta_{j}^{\top}X_{\beta^{\star},-j}/n||_{\infty}=O_{p}(\sqrt{\log p/n}), $$

by the union bound and the Hoeffding’s inequality. It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}I_{12} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}||\eta_{j}^{\top}X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}/n||_{\infty}\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\gamma}_{j}-\gamma_{j}||_{1} \displaystyle=O_{p}(s\log p/n). $$

For $I_{13}$ , since $\gamma_{j}$ is $s-$ sparse, by Assumption 4.2 (2), we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}||\gamma_{j}||_{1} \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{s}\max_{j\in[p]}||\gamma_{j}||_{2} \displaystyle=\sqrt{s}\max_{j\in[p]}[\Sigma_{j,-j}\Sigma_{-j,-j}^{-2}\Sigma_{-j,j}]^{1/2} \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{s}C_{1}^{2}/C_{2}. $$

In addition, by the KKT condition of the $j$ -th nodewise Lasso regression, we have

$$ \max_{j\in[p]}||X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}^{\top}\left(X_{\widehat{\beta},j}-X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right)/n||_{\infty}\leq\lambda_{j}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}I_{13} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}||\gamma_{j}||_{1}\max_{j\in[p]}||X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}^{\top}\left(X_{\widehat{\beta},j}-X_{\widehat{\beta},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}\right)/n||_{\infty} \displaystyle=O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n}). $$

For $I_{14}$ , we first notice that

$$ \displaystyle||X_{\beta^{\star},j}-X_{\beta^{\star},-j}\widehat{\gamma}_{j}||_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq||\eta_{j}||_{\infty}+||X_{\beta^{\star},-j}(\gamma_{j}-\widehat{\gamma}_{j})||_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq 2C_{1}+C_{1}||\gamma_{j}-\widehat{\gamma}_{j}||_{1} \displaystyle\leq 3C_{1} $$

by Assumption 4.2 (2) and Equation (166). By Assumption 4.2 (3), it follows that

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}I_{14} \displaystyle\leq\frac{3C_{1}^{2}}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left|\frac{\ddot{\rho}(x_{i}^{\intercal}\widehat{\beta})-\ddot{\rho}(x_{i}^{\intercal}\beta^{\star})}{\ddot{\rho}(x_{i}^{\intercal}\beta^{\star})}\right| \displaystyle=O_{p}(||X(\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star})||_{2}/\sqrt{n}) \displaystyle=O_{p}(\sqrt{p_{1}\log p/n}), $$

in which the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Combining the upper bound on $\max_{j\in[p]}I_{11}$ , $\max_{j\in[p]}I_{12}$ , $\max_{j\in[p]}I_{13}$ and $\max_{j\in[p]}I_{14}$ , we show that

$$ \max_{j\in[p]}I_{1}=O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n}). $$

Finally, $\max_{j\in[p]}I_{2}$ can be upper bounded similarly as $\max_{j\in[p]}I_{14}$ . This completes the proof of the first claim in Lemma A.19. The second claim follows by noticing that $1/\tau_{j}^{2}$ is uniformly upper bounded because

$$ 1/\tau_{j}^{2}=\Theta_{j,j}\leq\sigma_{\max}(\Theta)=1/\sigma_{\min}(\Sigma)\leq C_{2}. $$

This completes the proof of Lemma A.19

#### Lemma A.20.

Under Assumption 4.2, we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{1}=O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}), \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{2}=O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n}), \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}\Sigma\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}-\Theta_{j,j}|=O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n}). $$

Proof of Lemma A.20. By Lemma A.18 and A.19, for any $\epsilon>0$ , there exists a constant $C_{\epsilon}>0$ , such that $\mathbbm{P}(\cap_{i=1}^{6}E^{\epsilon}_{i})\geq 1-\epsilon$ , in which $E_{i}^{\epsilon}$ for $i\in[4]$ are specified in Lemma A.18, and

$$ \displaystyle E_{5}^{\epsilon}=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}\left|\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-\tau_{j}^{2}\right|\leq C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}\right\}, \displaystyle E_{6}^{\epsilon}=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}\left|1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-1/\tau_{j}^{2}\right|\leq C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}\right\}. $$

In the following, we condition on this high probability event $\cap_{i=1}^{6}E^{\epsilon}_{i}$ . By Assumption 4.2 (1), we assume that $n$ is large enough so that $C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}\leq C_{2}$ .

We first note that by Equation (176),

$$ 1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}\leq|1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-1/\tau_{j}^{2}|+1/\tau_{j}^{2}\leq 2C_{2}. $$

Thus, by Equation (170), we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{1} \displaystyle=\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{C}_{j,\cdot}/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-C_{j,\cdot}/\tau_{j}^{2}||_{1} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\gamma}_{j}-\gamma_{j}||_{1}\max_{j\in[p]}1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}+\max_{j\in[p]}||\gamma_{j}||_{1}\max_{j\in[p]}\left|1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-1/\tau_{j}^{2}\right| \displaystyle\leq 2C_{2}C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}+C_{1}^{2}/C_{2}C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s}\sqrt{s\log p/n} \displaystyle=O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}). $$

Similarly, we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{2} \displaystyle=\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{C}_{j,\cdot}/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-C_{j,\cdot}/\tau_{j}^{2}||_{2} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\gamma}_{j}-\gamma_{j}||_{2}\max_{j\in[p]}1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}+\max_{j\in[p]}||\gamma_{j}||_{2}\max_{j\in[p]}\left|1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-1/\tau_{j}^{2}\right| \displaystyle\leq 2C_{2}C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}+C_{1}^{2}/C_{2}C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n} \displaystyle=O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n}). $$

For the last claim in Lemma A.20, we employ the following decomposition.

$$ \displaystyle\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}\Sigma\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}-\Theta_{j,j} \displaystyle=(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})\Sigma(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})^{\top}+2\Theta_{j,\cdot}\Sigma(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})^{\top} \displaystyle:=I_{1}+I_{2}. $$

For $I_{1}$ , by Assumption 4.2 (2), we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}I_{1} \displaystyle\leq\sigma_{\max}(\Sigma)\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||^{2}_{2} \displaystyle=O_{p}(s\log p/n). $$

For $I_{2}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}I_{2} \displaystyle=2\max_{j\in[p]}e_{j}^{\top}(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})^{\top} \displaystyle=2\max_{j\in[p]}\left|1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-1/\tau_{j}^{2}\right| \displaystyle=O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n}). $$

This completes the proof of Lemma A.20.

#### Lemma A.21.

Under Assumption 4.2, we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}_{j}-\sigma_{j}|=O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}), \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}|1/\widehat{\sigma}_{j}-1/\sigma_{j}|=O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}). $$

Proof of Lemma A.21. By Assumption 4.2 (2), $\sigma^{2}=\Theta_{j,j}\geq\sigma_{\min}(\Theta)\geq 1/C_{2}>0$ . Therefore, we only need to consider the first claim in the lemma. In addition, since

$$ \max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}_{j}-\sigma_{j}|\leq\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}^{2}_{j}-\sigma^{2}_{j}|/\sigma_{j}\leq\sqrt{C_{2}}\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}^{2}_{j}-\sigma^{2}_{j}|, $$

it is sufficient to show that

$$ \max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}^{2}_{j}-\sigma^{2}_{j}|=O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}). $$

We note that

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}^{2}_{j}-\sigma^{2}_{j}| \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}\Sigma\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}-\Theta_{j,j}|+\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}\widehat{\Sigma}\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}-\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}\Sigma\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}|. $$

By Lemma A.20, the first term is $O_{p}(\sqrt{s\log p/n})$ . Using the same arguments as in the proof of Theorem 3.1 in Van de Geer et al., (2014) (page 1198), we can show that the second term is $O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n})$ . This completes the proof of Lemma A.21.

#### A.7.2 Proof of Proposition 4.2

We first note that for $j\in[p]$ , the bias term $\Delta_{j}$ can be decomposed into the following three terms,

$$ \displaystyle R_{1,j} \displaystyle=\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma_{j}}\Theta_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}-\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}, \displaystyle R_{2,j} \displaystyle=-\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}\left(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\ddot{\ell}_{\widehat{\beta}}-e_{j}^{\top}\right)(\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star}), \displaystyle R_{3,j} \displaystyle=-\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}P_{n}(\dot{\ell}_{\widehat{\beta}}-\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}})+\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}X^{\top}W^{2}_{\widehat{\beta}}X(\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star}). $$

We proceed to bound each term. For any $\epsilon>0$ , there exists a constant $C_{\epsilon}>0$ such that $\mathbbm{P}(\cap_{i=1}^{10}E_{i}^{\epsilon})\geq 1-\epsilon$ , in which $E_{i}^{\epsilon}$ for $i\in[4]$ are defined in Lemma A.18, $E_{5}^{\epsilon}$ and $E_{6}^{\epsilon}$ are defined in Lemma A.20, and $E_{7}^{\epsilon},E_{8}^{\epsilon},E_{9}^{\epsilon},E_{10}^{\epsilon}$ are defined as follows,

$$ \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{7}\hskip 2.84544pt=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{1}\leq C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}\right\}, \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{8}\hskip 2.84544pt=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{2}\leq C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}\right\}, \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{9}\hskip 2.84544pt=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}|\widehat{\sigma}_{j}-\sigma_{j}|\leq C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}\right\}, \displaystyle E^{\epsilon}_{10}=\left\{\max_{j\in[p]}|1/\widehat{\sigma}_{j}-1/\sigma_{j}|\leq C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}\right\}. $$

In the following, we condition on this high probability event $\cap_{i=1}^{10}E_{i}^{\epsilon}$ . By Assumption 4.2 (1), we further assume that $n,p$ are large enough so that $C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}\vee C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}\leq 1$ .

For $R_{1,j}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}R_{1,j} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}\left|\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma_{j}}\left(\Theta_{j,\cdot}-\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}\right)P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}\right|+\max_{j\in[p]}\left|\sqrt{n}\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}\left(\frac{1}{\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}-\frac{1}{\sigma_{j}}\right)\right| \displaystyle:=I_{1}+I_{2}. $$

For $I_{1}$ , since $\mathbbm{E}[P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}]=0$ and $||\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}||_{\infty}$ is upper bounded by Assumption 4.2 (2)(3), we have

$$ ||P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}||_{\infty}=O_{p}(\sqrt{\log p/n}) $$

using the union bound and the Hoeffding’s inequality. Since $\sigma^{2}\geq 1/C_{2}$ (see the proof of Lemma A.21), it follows that

$$ \displaystyle I_{1} \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{C_{2}}\sqrt{n}||P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}||_{\infty}\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot}||_{1} \displaystyle=\sqrt{n}O_{p}(\sqrt{\log p/n})O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}) \displaystyle=o_{p}(1) $$

by Assumption 4.2 (1). For $I_{2}$ , using the same argument, we have

$$ \displaystyle I_{2} \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{n}\max_{j\in[p]}||\widehat{\Theta}_{j}||_{\infty}||P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}||_{\infty}\max_{j\in[p]}\left|\frac{1}{\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}-\frac{1}{\sigma_{j}}\right| \displaystyle\leq\sqrt{n}\left(||\widehat{\Theta}-\Theta||_{\infty}+||\Theta||_{\infty}\right)O_{p}(\sqrt{\log p/n})O_{p}(s\sqrt{\log p/n}) \displaystyle=o_{p}(1). $$

For $R_{2,j}$ , using the KKT condition of the nodewise Lasso regression, we have

$$ \left|\left|\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\ddot{\ell}_{\widehat{\beta}}-e_{j}^{\top}\right|\right|_{\infty}\leq\lambda_{j}/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}. $$

Since

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}|1/\widehat{\tau}_{j}^{2}-1/\tau_{j}^{2}|+\max_{j\in[p]}1/\tau_{j}^{2} \displaystyle\leq C_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s\log p/n}+\max_{j\in[p]}1/\Theta_{j,j} \displaystyle\leq 1+C_{2} $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\max_{j\in[p]}1/\widehat{\sigma}_{j} \displaystyle\leq\max_{j\in[p]}|1/\widehat{\sigma}_{j}-1/\sigma_{j}|+\max_{j\in[p]}1/\sigma_{j} \displaystyle\leq C_{\epsilon}s\sqrt{\log p/n}+1/\sigma^{1/2}_{\min}(\Sigma) \displaystyle\leq 1+\sqrt{C_{2}} $$

by Assumption 4.2 (3), we have

$$ \displaystyle R_{2,j}\leq(1+C_{2})\sqrt{n}\left|\left|\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\ddot{\ell}_{\widehat{\beta}}-e_{j}^{\top}\right|\right|_{\infty}||\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star}||_{1}=o_{p}(1) $$

by Assumption 4.2 (1).

For $R_{3,j}$ , the first term is $o_{p}(1)$ following the proof of Theorem 3.1 in Van de Geer et al., (2014). For the second term, we note that

$$ \displaystyle||X\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}||_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq||X\Theta_{j,\cdot}^{\top}||_{\infty}+||X(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})^{\top}||_{\infty} \displaystyle\leq||X||_{\infty}+||X_{-j}\gamma_{j}||_{\infty}+||X||_{\infty}||(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})^{\top}||_{1} \displaystyle\leq||X||_{\infty}+||X_{\beta^{\star},-j}\gamma_{j}||_{\infty}/\inf|\ddot{\rho}(x^{\intercal}\beta^{\star})|+||X||_{\infty}||(\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}-\Theta_{j,\cdot})^{\top}||_{1} \displaystyle<+\infty $$

by Assumption 4.2 (2)(3). By the mean value Theorem and Assumption 4.2, it follows that

$$ R_{3,j}\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}\widehat{\sigma}_{j}}||X\widehat{\Theta}_{j,\cdot}^{\top}||_{\infty}||X(\widehat{\beta}-\beta^{\star})||_{2}^{2}=o_{p}(1). $$

This completes the proof of Proposition 4.2.

#### A.7.3 Proof of Proposition 4.3

The proof of Proposition 4.3 essentially follows the same as the proof of Proposition 4.1. The only change is that $Z_{j}=-{\sqrt{n}\Theta_{j,\cdot}P_{n}\dot{\ell}_{\beta^{\star}}}/{\sigma_{j}}$ is not exactly normal, but asymptotically normal. The discrepancy between the joint law of $(Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{p})$ and the corresponding multivariate normal distribution (with the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ ) can be quantified using the Berry-Esseen Theorem, which is in the order of $o(1/\sqrt{n})$ . Thus, we can establish the GLM version of Lemma A.15 similarly.
